direction: Strengthen the construction+improvement loop inside the hook: keep cheapest-insertion guided by score_insertion_move (regret/delta-based ordering with randomized tie-breaking to diversify restarts), then run a budget-aware 2-opt local search that (a) restricts candidate edges to a k-nearest-neighbor list built once from the distance matrix, (b) uses first-improvement with don't-look bits and a neighbor re-init queue, and (c) hands remaining time to repeated perturbation (double-bridge) + re-optimization, spending time proportional to n. Also add an Or-opt/segment-relocation pass on the same candidate lists since it is cheap and complements 2-opt on clustered/angular instances.

operations.mechanism: Cheapest-insertion is the documented strong TSP construction and the active template's allowed move hook is exactly score_insertion_move, so the biggest gains available within this interface come from (1) making insertion regret-based and randomized so multiple restarts explore different basins, and (2) upgrading the improvement phase to candidate-list (k-NN) 2-opt with don't-look bits rather than a full O(n^2) sweep, which is the classic Lin-Kernighan precursor efficiency trick; double-bridge perturbation gives an iterated-local-search structure that is known to dominate single-pass 2-opt at fixed cost. Postprocess is left at 'none' since the allowed mode list contains only 'none' and all improvements must live in the hook.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: On the 24-node heterogeneous dev suite, a hooks-based solver that couples randomized-greedy guided-insertion construction (score_insertion_move with regret-based delta selection and tie randomization across restarts) with neighbor-list 2-opt + Or-opt under a don't-look-bit first-improvement schedule and double-bridge restarts will substantially lower mean tour cost versus a plain guided-insertion-plus-full-2-opt baseline at the same 500 ms budget, because candidate-list restriction keeps each local-search pass O(n) per improving move and frees budget for extra restarts, improving the worst-case regime (clustered/angular) without hurting uniform-random ones.
